August opened with both majors down over 3%.

Bitcoin fell to roughly $62,869 (-3.25%), Ethereum to about $1,865 (-3.18%), and total crypto market cap slipped to $2.25T. Fear & Greed held at 27 — unchanged from a week ago, still squarely in Fear territory.

The Fed stopped pretending cuts were coming.

Three officials voted against holding rates this week — and all three wanted them higher. First unified triple dissent since September 2016.

Then the projections moved up: end-2026 expectations went from 3.25–3.75% to 3.6–4.1%.

Higher-for-longer isn't a risk scenario now. It's the base case.

The Fear & Greed Index is on every crypto headline. Almost nobody reads it correctly.

It's one number from 0 to 100, built from five weighted inputs:

→ Volatility — 25%
→ Market momentum and volume — 25%
→ Social media activity — 15%
→ Bitcoin dominance — 10%
→ Google Trends — 10%

Right now it reads 29. That's Fear.

Five things people get wrong about Bitcoin — and none of them are stupid questions.

🔴 "They can just print more" → Hard-capped at 21 million. That limit lives in the code every node runs. Changing it would require near-universal agreement from people voting to devalue their own holdings. The cap IS the product.

🔴 "You can reverse a transaction" → Once confirmed, it's permanent. No support desk. No chargeback. Send…

The most important crypto story this week isn't a price — it's a law.

The CLARITY Act is headed for a House vote. If it passes, the US finally gets an answer to the question that's haunted crypto for a decade: which tokens are securities, and which are commodities?
